topPlaces.name: Gujri Mahal
topPlaces.description: 14th-century baradari palace built by Sultan Firoz Shah Tughlaq for his beloved Gujri queen, featuring dark stone construction and nine intricately carved bays.

topPlaces.name: Lat Ki Masjid & Ashokan Pillar
topPlaces.description: Historic mosque within the palace courtyard featuring an ancient polished stone Ashokan pillar repurposed from an earlier Buddhist sanctuary.

image.alt: Lat Ki Masjid & Ashokan Pillar — Hisar, Haryana, India

topPlaces.name: Pranpir Badshah Tomb
topPlaces.description: Magnificent 14th-century domed red sandstone mausoleum set upon a raised platform, commemorating the revered Sufi spiritual guide Baba Pranpir.

image.alt: Pranpir Badshah Tomb — Hisar, Haryana, India

topPlaces.name: Blue Bird Lake
topPlaces.description: Lush wetland lake operated by Haryana Tourism, serving as a seasonal sanctuary for migratory waterfowl with boating decks and shaded picnic paths.

image.alt: Blue Bird Lake — Hisar, Haryana, India

topPlaces.name: St. Thomas Church, Hisar
topPlaces.description: 1860s Gothic revival Victorian church consecrated in the British cantonment era, noted for pointed stone arches, bell belfry, and stained glass windows.

image.alt: St. Thomas Church, Hisar — Hisar, Haryana, India

topPlaces.name: Hansi Fort (Asigarh Fort) & Barsi Gate
topPlaces.description: Ancient hill fortress attributed to Prithviraj Chauhan with the monumental 12th-century Barsi Gate displaying Sultanate archways and defensive bastions.

image.alt: Hansi Fort (Asigarh Fort) & Barsi Gate — Hisar, Haryana, India

topPlaces.name: Agroha Dham
topPlaces.description: Colossal temple complex and archaeological mound of ancient Agroha, showcasing towering shikhara architecture, marble courtyards, and holy sarovars.

topPlaces.name: Deer Park, Hisar
topPlaces.description: Peaceful 48-acre wildlife habitat maintained by the forest department, providing sanctuary to herds of blackbuck, spotted chital, and native woodland birds.

image.alt: Deer Park, Hisar — Hisar, Haryana, India

items.note: Blue Bird Lake, Hisar, is a resident and endangered migratory bird wetland habitat, lake and recreation area in the town of Hisar, in the Hisar district of Haryana State, India. Blue Bird Lake is close to Hisar Airport on NH-9 in Hisar, Haryana.

Mahavir Stadium, built in 1972, is a multipurpose sports complex located in Hisar city of Haryana, India. It has second largest capacity in Haryana, after the Shah Satnam Ji Cricket Stadium in Sirsa which has capacity of 35,000 spectators.
St. Thomas' Church is located in Hisar city of Haryana, India.

Pranpir Badshah's tomb (Hindi: बाबा प्राणपिर बादशाह), built from white material, near Mahabir Stadium in Hisar city of Haryana state in India, is claimed to be a 14th-century tomb of foreign-origin Islamic invader who as ghazi (title for Muslim warrior who kill non-Muslims in Ghazwatul-Hind furtherance of Islam) massacred native Indians, but the tomb itself, site and materials are originally of Hindu origin. There are social and legal campaigns to reclaim it as the Hindu temple, but hindered by the colonial mindset and antiquated laws of India which discriminate against the Indian-origin native religions in favour of foreign-origin religions of invaders and colonisers.
Government Polytechnic, Hisar is a public funded college located in Hisar in the Indian state of Haryana.

Old Court Commercial Complex is a commercial suburb located in Hisar city and Hisar Vidhan Sabha constituency of Haryana, India. The planning of this area is administered by Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA).
